name: Jeroboam the son of Joash
charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord forty-one years; departing not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
summary: Jeroboam the son of Joash reigned forty-one years in Samaria and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, yet the Lord used him to restore Israel’s border from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the plain, as Jonah had prophesied, because He saw how bitter Israel’s affliction was (2 Kings 14:23-27). The prosperity of his reign bred luxury, oppression and violence, and Amos and Hosea prophesied the sword against his house and captivity for Israel (Amos 7:9-11; Hosea 1:4). The sentence fell on his son Zachariah, killed after six months, the end of Jehu’s fourth generation (2 Kings 15:8-12).
offenseFull: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash began to reign in Samaria and reigned forty-one years, one year longer than David; the teaching dates him about 793 to 753 BC (2 Kings 14:23). He did evil and did not depart from any of the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat (2 Kings 14:24). Like Omri, he looms large in secular history and gets about six verses in scripture; the Lord does not care about carnal accolades.

His reign was prosperous, and riches bred trouble: more money, more problems. Amos railed against the rich who sold the upright for money and the needy for the price of sandals, and against those at ease in Zion (Amos 2:6-8; Amos 6:1); they were about making their bread, impatient for the Sabbath to end so they could sell (Amos 8:5). Whoever oppresses the poor to increase his riches will come to want (Proverbs 22:16). Hosea described the land in those days: no truth, no mercy, no knowledge of God, but swearing, lying, killing and stealing, and blood touching blood (Hosea 4:1-2). The Lord eased the pressure from outside, and the northern kingdom decided to relax too.

Amos prophesied that the sanctuaries of Israel would be laid waste and the Lord would rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword. Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to the king that Amos was conspiring against him and the land could not bear his words, and told the prophet to go back to Judah and prophesy there (Amos 7:9-13). He misreported him: Amos said the sword would come on the house of Jeroboam, not that Jeroboam himself would die by it. The prophet’s job is the word of the Lord, no more and no less, and Amos was telling the northern kingdom they were going into slavery soon.
judgmentFull: He restored Israel’s border from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the plain, according to the word the Lord spoke by His servant Jonah the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25). The entrance of Hamath is the northern border of the land given in Numbers, reached under David and Solomon, and the sea of the plain is the Salt Sea (Numbers 34:8; Deuteronomy 3:17). Jonah of Gath-hepher was of Zebulun, and he, Hosea and Amos prophesied in the same days. The Lord saw that Israel’s affliction was very bitter, with no one left, bond or free, and no helper, and He had not said He would blot out the name of Israel, so He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam (2 Kings 14:26-27). It was not because they were righteous, but because He saw their oppression. He recovered Damascus and Hamath and made Syria tributary (2 Kings 14:28).

The sentence was deferred, not lifted. Hosea’s first child was named Jezreel, because the Lord would soon punish the house of Jehu for the blood of Jezreel and end the kingdom of Israel (Hosea 1:1, 4). Jeroboam slept with his fathers, and his son Zachariah reigned six months, doing evil as his fathers had, until Shallum conspired against him and killed him before the people; that was the word the Lord spoke to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne to the fourth generation (2 Kings 14:29; 2 Kings 15:8-12). After him came violence, men slaying each other for the throne; an unwise king destroys his people (Ecclesiasticus 10:3). The teacher applies it to America: destruction is coming to this land.

text.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gath–hepher.
For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel.
And the Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.
And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zachariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
And the rest of the acts of Zachariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
This was the word of the Lord which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes;
That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the meek: and a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name:
And they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.
Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria, which are named chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel came!
Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?
He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.
By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.
And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.

He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gath–hepher.
From mount Hor ye shall point out your border unto the entrance of Hamath; and the goings forth of the border shall be to Zedad:
The plain also, and Jordan, and the coast thereof, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, under Ashdoth–pisgah eastward.
For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel.
And the Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
The word of the Lord that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.
An unwise king destroyeth his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.
